title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.14333v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying "both are bad" rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model's share of decisive votes is flat. translated_title: AI并没有变笨，是我们变得更挑剔了：大型语言模型人类评估标准的不断上升
translated_abstract: 用户经常抱怨像ChatGPT这样的AI助手正在变差。某些版本确实会变化，但人类评估留下了第二种未经检验的可能性：评判者本身可能发生了变化。我们在Chatbot Arena平台上区分这两种因素——这是一个公开平台，人们在这里比较两个匿名大型语言模型（LLM）的回答，并选择更好的一个或判定两者都不好。我们研究了2023年5月至2024年8月期间针对版本固定模型对投出的1,260,967张盲选票，这些模型包括带有日期标记的厂商快照模型和固定开源权重的模型。对于同一对未发生变化的模型，判定“两个都不好”的投票比例每月上升1.71个百分点（平均值为17.1%），而在2024年每月上升1.91个百分点。在2023年和2024年均被频繁观察到的十四对模型中，这一比例在每一对中都出现了上升，从15.5%升至23.3%。模型排名并未呈现趋势：2024年，更强模型在决定性投票中的份额保持平稳。这种上升在同一投票者内部同样成立（原文在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该研究通过分析Chatbot Arena上126万余张针对固定版本模型的盲投票数据发现，“两个都不好”的投票比例持续显著上升，表明AI模型并非在变差，而是人类评估者的标准在不断提高。
en_tdlr: Analyzing over 1.26 million blind votes on Chatbot Arena for pairs of fixed-version models, this study finds that the "both are bad" vote share steadily rises, showing that AI isn't getting worse—human evaluators' standards are becoming stricter.
